metadata.name: Esophageal Cancer (10-year)

sources.citation: Barrett's Esophagus and Esophageal Adenocarcinoma Risk

metadata.description: 10-year risk of esophageal cancer, including both adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma

caseFatality10yr.basis: SEER 5-year relative survival 22.2% (all stages, 2016-2022) -> CFR 0.778; relative survival nets out background mortality (10-year survival is modestly lower, so this is a slight underestimate)
caseFatality10yr.citation: SEER Cancer Stat Facts, National Cancer Institute

curves.notes: Esophageal cancer incidence; adenocarcinoma rising in Western populations
Esophageal cancer incidence; adenocarcinoma rising in Western populations

riskFactors.name: GERD (Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease)

mapping.notes: Chronic GERD is major risk factor for adenocarcinoma

riskFactors.citation: Rubenstein JH, Taylor JB. Meta-analysis: the association of oesophageal adenocarcinoma with symptoms of gastro-oesophageal reflux. Aliment Pharmacol Ther. 2010;32(10):1222-1227
riskFactors.notes: Weekly GERD symptoms: OR 4.92 (3.90-6.22) for esophageal ADENOcarcinoma (daily 7.40). The 2.5 here is diluted because the model covers combined EAC+SCC and GERD is not an SCC risk factor.

riskFactors.name: Barrett's Esophagus
riskFactors.notes: Barrett's esophagus HR~10-40 for esophageal adenocarcinoma; surveillance recommended

riskFactors.name: Smoking Status
riskFactors.citation: Wang QL, Xie SH, Li WT, Lagergren J. Smoking Cessation and Risk of Esophageal Cancer by Histological Type: systematic review and meta-analysis. J Natl Cancer Inst. 2017;109(12):djx115
riskFactors.notes: Adenocarcinoma: current RR 2.32 (1.96-2.75), former 1.62 (1.40-1.87); squamous: current 4.18 (3.42-5.12), former 2.05 (1.71-2.45). Values here sit between the histology-specific estimates for the combined outcome.

riskFactors.name: Alcohol Consumption

mapping.notes: Heavy drinking increases squamous cell carcinoma risk

riskFactors.citation: IARC Monographs on the Identification of Carcinogenic Hazards to Humans, Volume 100E: Personal Habits and Indoor Combustions (alcohol and oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma)
riskFactors.notes: Alcohol is an established cause of esophageal SQUAMOUS cell carcinoma with strong dose-response; adenocarcinoma shows no association (Tramacere meta: RR 0.87-0.96). Slope reflects the SCC component of the combined outcome.

riskFactors.name: Body Mass Index (Obesity)
riskFactors.citation: Turati F, et al. A meta-analysis of body mass index and esophageal and gastric cardia adenocarcinoma. Ann Oncol. 2013;24(3):609-617
riskFactors.notes: EAC: overweight RR 1.71 (1.50-1.96), obese RR 2.34 (1.95-2.81). Values here are attenuated because BMI is inversely associated with the SCC component of the combined outcome.
